input: Create a color-coded family chore rotation calendar

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of family members and their ages (especially kids vs. adults) directly determines how many color tracks are needed and what chores are age-appropriate to assign.
The specific list of chores to include — and which to exclude — defines the entire content of the calendar; without it, the plan could be too sparse or overwhelming.
The rotation cadence (daily, weekly, bi-weekly, monthly) shapes the calendar's structure completely — a daily chart looks and works very differently from a weekly one.
The format and tool used (printed paper chart, Google Sheets, a whiteboard, an app) determines what is actually built and handed over to the user.
Any hard limits — such as certain members being unavailable on specific days, or chores that must always be done by one person — would override the rotation logic.
Whether the color-coding should map to people, chore categories, or difficulty level changes the entire visual design and legend system of the calendar.
Knowing whether success means equal time distribution, fair difficulty distribution, or simply that everyone knows their job each week determines how the rotation algorithm is validated.

gold.taskTitle: Build a color-coded family chore rotation calendar
gold.taskDescription: Create a visual, color-coded calendar that rotates chore assignments among family members on a recurring schedule.

questions.title: How many family members will have chores assigned?
questions.description: Identify the total number of people and their approximate ages so the right number of color tracks can be created and age-appropriate chores can be assigned.

questions.title: Which specific chores should be included in the rotation?
questions.description: Gather the exact list of household chores to appear on the calendar, as well as any that should be permanently excluded or kept off-rotation.

questions.title: How often should chore assignments rotate — daily or weekly?
questions.description: Determine the rotation cadence (daily, weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly) since this fundamentally shapes the calendar's structure and layout.

questions.title: What format should the finished calendar be in?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants a printable chart, a digital spreadsheet, a whiteboard template, or an app-based solution so the right deliverable is built.

questions.title: Are any family members exempt from certain chores or days?
questions.description: Capture hard constraints such as a young child who cannot do certain tasks, a parent unavailable on weekends, or chores that must always belong to one person.

questions.title: Should each color represent a person, a chore type, or a difficulty level?
questions.description: Decide what the color-coding system actually maps to, since this drives the entire visual design, legend, and how the calendar is read at a glance.

questions.title: What does a fair or successful rotation look like to you?
questions.description: Understand whether success means equal time spent on chores, balanced difficulty across members, or simply clear visibility of who does what each week.
